subject: Clarify security exhibit: SOC 2 evidence windows & pen-test access

Subject: Security exhibit: evidence windows and pen-test access - clarification

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA/Order Form. A couple of items from Acme's security team we need to confirm before routing to procurement:

- SOC 2 evidence: we need to understand the cadence for sharing SOC 2 artifacts (reports, complementary user-entity controls) and the expected SLA for responses to evidence requests. Are you proposing a quarterly evidence bundle or ad-hoc requests?

- Penetration test: the security exhibit references a "reasonable notice" window for pen tests. Can you clarify minimum notice (we generally want a 30-day window) and whether Redwood will provide a staging environment with equivalent config and test accounts?

- Data retention & logs: sample retention periods for auth logs and audit trails (we'd like to map to our 90/365 requirement).

Would appreciate an allocation of who on your side will be the primary evidence contact, and a short timeline for when you can provide a redline that addresses those bullets. We're scheduling procurement review next Thursday, so a quick turn would help.

Thanks,
Samir

Subject: Re: Security exhibit: evidence windows and pen-test access - clarification

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. See inline and attached: I pushed an initial redline to the order form and a proposed security exhibit (attachments). Short answers here and next steps below.

- SOC 2 evidence cadence: we propose a primary annual SOC 2 Type II report delivery (standard) plus an "evidence-on-request" workflow for scoped requests. For routine onboarding evidence (configuration guides, SOC mapping), we can provide a quarterly evidence bundle for customers with enterprise SLAs. SLA for ad-hoc requests: we can commit to initial acknowledgement within 3 business days and a substantive response within 10 business days for standard items (logs, configurations). For deep forensic artifacts we may need 20 business days.

- Pen-test notice & staging: Redwood is proposing a minimum 21-calendar-day notice in the current exhibit, but we're open to 30 days for a production-impacting test. We can provide a staging environment that mirrors customer production configuration for a subset of tenants; access provisioning will require an NDA + test scoping form. We also propose a rule that tests causing service-impacting outages are not permitted without explicit change-window coordination.

- Retention: auth and audit logs are retained 90 days in hot storage and 365 days in cold storage by default. We can expose a retention SLA in the security exhibit and offer an extended retention add-on for longer-term retention.

Next steps: Vanessa / Legal to review the redline and exhibit (cc'd). I've attached: redline_MSA_orderform_20260501.pdf and security_exhibit_draft_v3.docx. If that looks good I can convert to DocuSign-ready Order Form and we can schedule a 30-minute evidence-handoff call next week.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Karthik / team — quick legal comments after scanning the redline:

1) Pen-test window: accept 30-day minimum notice for production-impacting tests; add explicit requirement for a scoped test plan and a point of contact for test ops. Suggest language: "Customer shall provide a written test plan and designate a technical point of contact at least thirty (30) calendar days prior to any penetration test against Redwood-managed environments."

2) Staging access: propose limited staging access for third-party testers with timeboxed credentials (max 7 days per engagement) and MFA enforced. Add a clause that all tester accounts are subject to Redwood's acceptable use and that Redwood will monitor and terminate sessions if risk indicators are triggered.

3) Evidence SLA: propose the following matrix be added to the exhibit: acknowledge within 3 business days; basic artifacts (config docs, sample logs) within 10 business days; full forensic requests (requires legal review) within 20 business days or as otherwise agreed.

4) KMS/HSM language: Acme asked about KMS/HSM. Add optional language for Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for customers on Private/Dedicated deployments and standard KMS integration notes for hosted.

I'm attaching a short snippet to insert into the exhibit (security_exhibit_draft_v3.docx). Once we align, I'll prepare a redline to the Order Form focused only on Exhibit + Order Form paragraph that ties to the add-on pricing for extended retention.

Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Hi all — Lumina (counsel for Acme on this deal) had a couple of cleanups after reviewing the draft exhibit:

- Please replace the phrase "reasonable notice" with an explicit 30-day notice for production pen-tests (we agree with Vanessa's snippet).

- For the evidence SLA, Lumina requests an explicit exclusion list for what falls under "full forensic" to avoid indefinite discovery cycles. Suggested exclusions: ephemeral debug logs, per-tenant encrypted payloads (unless court order), and raw KV cache contents.

- BYOK: Lumina wants confirmation that key management for BYOK will not require Redwood to hold key material; please confirm operationally how key rotation/termination would be handled on Dedicated vs Hosted.

Also, two administrative asks: can you provide a single consolidated PDF with the final Exhibit + the Order Form redline, and can you send a DocuSign-ready Order Form once language is locked? Procurement needs DocuSign to start approval routing.

Thanks,
Maya Chen

Thanks all — agreed items and plan below, and I've linked the shared Drive folder with the working artifacts.

Agreed items:
- Pen test: final language to require 30-calendar-day notice for production-impacting pentests; staging tests allowed with 14-day notice and timeboxed creds (7 days).
- Evidence SLA: we'll insert the 3/10/20 business-day matrix and add the Lumina-requested exclusion list.
- BYOK: confirm that BYOK is supported for Dedicated/Private (customer holds key material; Redwood receives wrapped keys and does not retain plaintext). We'll document rotation/termination flows in the exhibit appendix.
